description: Mutated HTTP/2 frame attack against an externally-launched H2C (HTTP/2 cleartext) target. Seed: a single HEADERS frame plus DATA frame for GET /plaintext, mutated by radamsa into invalid frame headers, malformed HPACK blocks, and oversized payloads. Each variant is fired over a fresh TCP connection that starts with the H2C connection preface. PRIMARY CHECK: after attack window + cooldown, target serves clean GET /health with HTTP/2 200 within 1s.
loopback_caveat: H2C cleartext only; H2-over-TLS not covered by this scenario. transport_mode=loopback-h2 mandatory.

attack_profile.rate_note: requests_per_second is a REQUESTED rate. Until 2026-08-26 the driver was single-threaded and every read timeout blocked it for the full socket deadline, so the first campaign requested 500 and achieved 3.4 (60 timeouts x 2.0 s consumed the whole 120 s window; radamsa generation was 1.1 % of it). The driver now fires from a worker pool and reports achieved_rps and backlog_skips -- a run that cannot reach this rate says so instead of letting this number stand in for what happened.
attack_profile.concurrency_note: Concurrency is part of the stimulus, not a harness detail: N connections at once is a different attack from N in sequence. It travels with the result and belongs in any comparison. Sizing: rps x incomplete-mutant fraction x socket timeout gives the worker-seconds per wall second the timeouts alone consume.

liveness_probe.note: Liveness probe uses curl --http2-prior-knowledge. nghttp may be used as fallback.

tolerance.hang_note: hang_count counts read timeouts on mutants whose frame sequence ended on a frame boundary, where the target owed an answer. A mutant with a truncated final frame leaves the target correctly waiting: incomplete-wait, not a hang.

comparison_axis_note: Cross-stack comparison requires identical --radamsa-seed AND identical H2 server-side limits (max-concurrent-streams, max-frame-size, max-header-list-size). Different limits change what gets rejected at the protocol layer vs the parser layer.
